question:
Let \(f:N\to N\) be the function defined by \(f(0)=0\), \(f(1)=1\), and \(f(n)=f(n-1)+f(n-2)\) for \(n\ge2\), where \(N\) is the set of all non-negative integers. Prove the following results:

(i) \(f(n)<f(n+1)\) for all \(n\ge2\).

(ii) There exist precisely four non-negative integers \(n\) for which \(f(f(n))=f(n)\).

(iii) \(f(5n)\) is divisible by 5, for all \(n\).

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
